newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND UNDER DOUBLE PRESSURE AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND UNDER DOUBLE PRESSURE AT HOME.

text.p: World Cup downhill champion Luc Alphand will be under intense pressure this weekend when he starts his bid for a third successive title on home snow in Val d'Isere.

The 31-year-old Frenchman and other speed specialists have good reasons to feel fidgety, having made abortive journeys to the United States earlier this month when the scheduled opening downhill and Super-G fell victim to heavy snow falls.
The rescheduling makes the Val d'Isere race even more significant for Alphand who triumphed here last year to become the first Frenchman to win a World Cup downhill in the Savoy resort.

A second victory on the Oreiller-Killy piste would make him only the fourth skier to win a downhill twice in Jean-Claude Killy's home village and only the second to score back to back wins here after Austrian Helmut Hoeflehner in 1990.

A lot is at stake as well for Alphand's compatriot Carole Montillet, one of the sensations of the early season with two podium places in a downhill in Lake Louise and a super-G in Vail earlier this month.
But World Cup leader Katja Seizinger of Germany has even more to defend, having won the three races held last season in Val d'Isere -- one downhill and three Super-G's.
Women lead the way in four days of racing in the French Alps with a downhill and a super-G, the men following over the weekend in the same events.

As usual on a piste which is one of their favourite on the circuit, Austrians should be Alphand's leading rivals in the downhill. World champion Patrick Ortlieb, who won Olympic gold in the same resort but on a different piste in 1992, should again be near the podium.

Last year, Alphand beat Roland Assinger and Hannes Trinkl but he should beware this time of suprise 1994 winner Joseph Strobl, who showed he was back in form with a giant slalom victory in Park City. Norwegians Lasse Kjus and Kjetil-Andre Aamodt are also men to watch.
The women's World Cup schedule has been less upset than the men's so far this season and Seizinger should know by now who her main rivals are.

Young Austrian Renate Goetschl confirmed what a fine all-rounder she was by winning the first downhill of her career last week in Vail. She was second and third behind Seizinger in the two super-G's held in Val d'Isere last year and obviously likes the course.
Montillet and Italian super-G world champion Isolde Kostner should be among other skiers to shine, allong with Swede Pernilla Wiberg, apparently in the best form of her life.
Russian Svetlana Gladishiva, rewarded with her first World Cup victory last week in Vail after seasons on the circuit, will also be aiming to prove she's not just a one-hit wonder.
Organisers were confident the races could go ahead as planned after heavy snow fell in the French Alps last week. Cold but dry weather was expected on race days.
